steps.description:
How does a programmer know where to start when building a large and complex program? The trick lies in how you break it down and plan your code sequence. That is why you are practising doing short codes. All large programs should be broken down in short parts which can be implemented like the way you have been doing. 

How do you you break a program down into smaller parts then? The are different methods. One convenient way is to write down the sequence of events are tackle them one by one in order.

The Comment block is useful for adding descriptions to your code. It does not perform any action.


Using Comment block is one quick way to help you plan your program and make your code readable!


Your good friend has just opened a small but high-tech restaurant. He has asked for your help to program a Robot Server.


The Robot Server should work as follows:

  • The tables are marked with colour codes.
  • The robot will wait in the kitchen. When the food is ready, the chef will select the color of the destination table and press a button to send the robot out.
  • The robot will deliver the food to the correct table (based on its colour) and then return to its original position in the kitchen.

You got the idea and have to test it out using the virtual robot as shown.

   

This might turn into a lengthy code. Let’s explore how to break the problem into smaller steps.

The first thing is to observe the sequence of events and list them down using Comment blocks. Below shows you how you can start.

 

Write down the remaining steps (you can have different number of Comment blocks). We will start programming in the next step.

We learnt earlier that we can plan our code by using Comment blocks to list down the sequence of actions.

After forming the sequence, we can start coding them in order. Below shows an example.


Note that it is normal that you may make amendments along the way.
